pages.name: Taking away
pages.text: To take `b` away from `a`, turn `b` round and add it nose to tail. With `a` = `5i + 2j` and `b` = `1i + 3j`, that gives `a − b` = `4i − 1j`. Drawn from one tail, the same arrow runs from the nose of `b` to the nose of `a`. Go out along `b`, then along `a − b`, and you land on `a`.

pages.name: Take 2i − 1j from 3i + 4j
pages.task: Here `a` is `3i + 4j` and `b` is `2i − 1j`. What is `a − b`?
pages.why: Turned round, `b` is `−2i + 1j`. Across, 3 − 2 = 1. Up, 4 + 1 = 5. So `a − b` is `1i + 5j`. Add `b` back on, and you land on `a`.

pages.name: Buoy to buoy
pages.text: A move from one point to another is a [[displacement]]. It is where you end minus where you started. Buoy A sits at `1i + 2j` km. Its arrow from the origin, `a`, is its [[position vector]]. Buoy B sits at `6i + 5j` km, with position vector `b`. So the move AB is `b − a`, which is `5i + 3j` km. Go out along `a`, then along AB, and you land on B.

pages.name: In line
pages.text: A, B and C sit at `1i + 1j`, `3i + 2j` and `7i + 4j`. AB is `2i + 1j`. BC is `4i + 2j`, which is 2 × AB. So the two steps point the same way. Parallel steps alone could sit on two separate lines. These two share B, so the three points lie on one line. They are [[collinear]]. Two copies of AB fit exactly along BC.

pages.name: Which point is in line?
pages.task: A sits at `1i + 1j` and B at `3i + 2j`. Which point lies on the line through A and B?
pages.why: AB is `2i + 1j`. From B to `9i + 5j` is `6i + 3j`, which is 3 × AB. The two steps share B, so the point is on the line.

pages.name: The boat and the stream
pages.text: A boat heads straight across at 4 m/s in a 3 m/s stream. Over the ground it moves along the sum of the two arrows, at 5 m/s, and lands downstream. To land opposite, it aims upstream until its upstream part cancels the stream. Aimed 48.59° upstream, it crosses at 2.65 m/s and lands on the target.

pages.name: Straight across
pages.task: A boat makes 5 m/s through the water in a 3 m/s stream. It aims upstream to cross straight over. What is its speed across?
pages.why: Its upstream part cancels the 3 m/s stream. The heading, 5 m/s, is the long side of a right-angled triangle. So the across part is `√(5² − 3²) = 4` m/s.

pages.why: Its across part is 4 m/s, so it crosses in 40 ÷ 4 = 10 s. All that time the stream carries it 3 m each second. So it lands 3 × 10 = 30 m downstream. Its track is 50 m long.
